q: 1. Two contour lines, having the same may cross each other only in the case of
explain: Two contour lines of the same elevation can unite (coincide/merge) together in special cases such as at a vertical cliff, though they do not typically cross transversely.

q: 2. Closed contours of decreasing values toward their centre, represent
explain: When closed contour loops show decreasing elevation values toward the centre, they represent a depression (low point), as opposed to a hill where values increase toward the centre.

q: 3. In route surveys, the most suitable method of contouring is
explain: For route surveys (roads, railways), the cross-section method of contouring is most suitable, since cross-sections perpendicular to the alignment naturally provide the elevation data needed for design.

q: 4. The horizontal equivalent which is a term generally uses in contoured map is
options: the least distance between two consecutive contours
the greatest distance between two consecutive contours
the mean distance between two consecutive contours
explain: As per the book's answer key, the horizontal equivalent in a contoured map is generally taken as the mean distance between two consecutive contours (representing the average ground slope over that interval).

q: 5. A pass or a saddle in a mountainous region
options: the lowest point of the ridge lines coincides with the highest point of the valley point
explain: A pass/saddle in mountainous terrain is characterized by all these features together - it lies between two ridge lines, connects two valleys, and represents the point where the lowest point of the ridge meets the highest point of the intervening valley - so all of these apply.

q: 6. Which one of the following methods can be used for contour interpolation?
explain: Contour interpolation between plotted spot levels can be performed using any of several methods - estimation, arithmetical calculation, or graphical means - so all of these are valid approaches.

q: 7. In direct method of contouring, the process of locating or identifying points lying on a contour is called
explain: In the direct method of contouring, the process of locating points that lie exactly on a particular contour in the field is called ranging (tracing the contour).

q: 8. In indirect method of contouring, the best method of interpolation if contours
explain: For the indirect method of contouring, contour interpolation between spot levels can be done using any of these methods - graphical, estimation, or arithmetical calculation - so all of these are valid.
